Last modified 27 July 2026

Abstracts

John Backus explored a sequence of applicative, functional and function-level languages starting before 1969 and continuing until he retired in 1991. The goal of this project is to preserve the surviving materials from this research and to put them into context. Comments, suggestions, and donations of additional materials are greatly appreciated.

The software crisis

In the late 1960s the "software crisis" became a frequent topic of discussion. Computers had become much more capable in speed and memory sizes and prices had come down, but as ambitions grew, a number of programming projects suffered from cost and shedule overruns and poor reliability. A pair of NATO-sponsored conferences on Software Engineering in 1968 and 1969 brought attention to the problems and served as an initial forum for discussing solutions, which included formal methods, design methodologies, and management techniques.

Although John Backus attended neither of these conferences, they resonated with his long-held desire to simplify the task of programming. He'd had early success with his Speedcoding and FORTRAN projects. FORTRAN in particular revolutionized the task of writing numerically-oriented programs, in many cases allowing scientists and engineers to write programs rivalling or exceeding the performance of programs written by professional programmers—members of the "priesthood," as Backus sometimes referred to them. After FORTRAN, he participated in the Algol project, and in 1963 was named an IBM Fellow in 1963, giving him the flexibility to choose any problem to work on. He then spent a number of years working on four color conjecture (now theorem). But somewhere around 1967–1969, Backus decided to take another try at the programming problem:

"I was just trying to think of some sort of really higher level programming that wasn’t as difficult as Fortran. The problem was that the idea of functional programming, the 'combining forms' and stuff like that, came pretty easily. But trying to make it into a real full system where you could deal with all the other issues that you couldn’t express in that language got very confusing and messy." [Booch2007]

Launching a project

For several years, Backus worked mostly alone on this new idea. Ted Codd consulted with him briefly, but that didn't last [Booch2007]. In late 1969, Dines Bjørner began working with him, first explaining the details of lambda-calculus and Curry's Combinatory Logic, then writing an interpreter (in PL/I) based on “finite state tree-transformer” semantic for Backus's language (which was then called RedSys) [Bjørner2025, 1972]. Bjørner worked with Backus until 1972, when they parted ways; Bjørner went on to work with Ted Codd [Bjørner2025], [BjørnerEtAl1973].

Backus's first publication was a 1972 research report titled "Reduction languages and variable-free programming"; the report acknowledges Bjørner "for writing a program to reduce Red items which was used to test some of the operators in this paper."[Backus1972a] This report introduced a family of expression-oriented languages with semantics given by simple rewrite rules. The featured language, called Red for reduction, was similiar in size to Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960], but rather than defining a function by describing its effect on the formal parameters, the programmer built up a function from a set of base functions using a function composition operator as well as a set of combining forms (here known as 'modifiers'). Each function took one (implicit) argument, which could be a sequence. This led to a programming style somewhat reminiscent of APL's "one-liners", and Backus later cited APL as an inspiration. During 1972, Phil Summers (then probably a graduate student intern from Yale, later an IBM researcher) did an experimental implementation of Red in Lisp [Summers1972].

This first report was fairly mild in its claims about Red, which he positioned more as a formal system than a practical programming language. In 1973 he followed up with a paper,presented at the first ACM Principles of Programming Languages conference [Backus1973a, c]. It refined the hierarchy of languages, presented a tidied-up version of Red as the centerpiece and concluded: "Hopefully, this work will lead to a semantic theory for a new class of programming languages, one which possesses an axiomatic foundation of the simplicity required for rigorous mathematical treatment."

During 1973, Backus went on the lecture circuit, giving 14 lectures at universities and research labs across the country [Backus1973d]. His annual report as an IBM Fellow described that year's work on language frameworks and the Red language, and then made two claims [Backus1974a]:

  1. "Simple, whole-entity programming languages, as contrasted to conventional complex, word-at-a-time programming languages, have the potential for drastically reducing the cost of programming.
  2. Present efforts to clean up and extend conventional concepts of programming languages have no such potential; ... indeed they will continue to add complexity to languages without dealing with the word-at-a-time problem, as they have for the past 15 years, and thereby actually increase the cost of programming and the expertise required for its practice. (Thus PL/I is perhaps 10 times as complex as Fortran, less economical in execution, and only 20-30% more powerful in expressiveness.)"

He concluded, "If there is any truth to the two assertions above, then Research should ask itself whether it has fallen into a comfortable but mistaken orthodoxy with respect to programming languages. I believe it should re-evaluate its emphasis and goals in computer science and programming; at least IBM computer scientists should be aware that reducing the cost of programming would do more to help IBM's growth than perhaps any other technical, accomplishment." In support of these claims, he introduced the phrase "von Neumann bottleneck"—the word-at-a-time nature of conventional computers—and argued that this carried over to the design of conventional programming languages, leading to their inefficiency and complexity.

It fell to Patricia Goldberg, Manager of the Automatic Programming group at IBM's Watson Research Center, to respond to Backus [Goldberg1974]. She agreed with the criticality of reducing the cost of programming, the need to go beyond languages of the "PL/I genre," the significance of APL, and the importance of discovering aggregate operations in various fields. But she noted, "I am not, however, convinced that we ought altogether to dispense with the notion of an explicit store and an assignment operator." She pointed out ongoing work at IBM on non-von Neumann frameworks as well as attempts to integrate these into useful programming systems. Backus responded with a vigorous reiteration of the need for IBM Research to study language frameworks with the goal of defining a very simple framework supporting rich definitions [Backus1974b].

Another assistant

Despite the lukewarm response from research management, Backus persevered. In the "Plans for 1974" section of his 1973 annual report, Backus had mentioned, "If time and assistance permit, I hope to begin work on an optimizing interpreter for Red languages." He let it be known he was interested in hiring someone to work with him , and Jim Gray, then at IBM San Jose Research and knowing I was looking for permanent employment, introduced me to Backus. I'd attended one of his lectures at UC Berkeley in 1972 and signed up for his mailing list, so I'd received and at least partially digested his two research reports. I'd also worked on interpreters for Snobol4 and APL. For the next 15 months or so, I worked with Backus to refine the language and to explore implementation ideas, including writing some experimental interpreters in Lisp and Mcg, an ISWIM-like language designed by W. H. Burge [Burge1968]. I gave a short talk to the department shortly after joining [McJones1974b] and wrote a technical report on "A Church-Rosser Property of Closed Application Languages" [McJones1975]. During this time Backus and I explored a series of minor variations on the Red language—see [Backus1974b] through [Backus1975b]. Work on the algebra of programs (first mentioned in [Backus1974a]) and modeling state transformations also begin. Sensing that the language was still in flux and the emphasis was more on formal methods than actual implementation, I eventually moved over to the System R relational database project.

During this period several researchers at universities began projects based on Backus's ideas. Klaus Berkling initiated design work at GMD in Germany for a reduction-based machine influenced by [Backus1973c]; it is said the be the first reduction machine actually implemented [Berkling1975], [Kluge1983]. Also Gyula A. Magó at the University of North Carolina initiated the FFPM project [Magó1976]. [Partain1989] describes these and other graph reduction machines.

The Turing Lecture

John Backus received the 1977 ACM Turing Award "For profound, influential, and lasting contributions to the design of practical high-level programming systems, notably through his work on FORTRAN, and for seminal publication of formal procedures for the specification of programming languages." His award lecture "Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style? A Functional Style and Its Algebra of Programs" was published in the Communications of the ACM, received by all ACM members [Backus1978b]. He argued:

"Conventional programming languages are growing ever more enormous, but not stronger. Inherent defects at the most basic level cause them to be both fat and weak: their primitive word-at-a-time style of programming, inherited from their common ancestor—the von Neumann computer, their close coupling of semantics to state transitions, their division of programming into a world of expressions and a world of statements, their inability to effectively use powerful combining forms for building new programs from existing ones, and their lack of useful mathematical properties for reasoning about programs."

The alternative he proposed was an "informal" functional programming language FP (with a related "formal" version FFP), an algebra of functional programs, and a framework for applicative state transitions (AST) for modeling history-sensitive systems. FP included a set of primitive functions for working with numbers, atoms, and sequences, as well as a set of combining forms for constructing more complex functions from simpler ones. Here's an example function for matrix multiplication:

Def MM ≡ (ααIP) ○ (αdistl) ○ distr ○ [1st, trans ○ 2nd]

○ represents function composition, α applies a function to each element of a sequence, and [,...,] applies a list of functions to a value, producing a sequence of results. MM expects a pair of compatible matrices, each represented as a sequences of rows. Reading from right to left, the function in brackets transposes the second matrix while leaving the first matrix intact. distr pairs a copy of the transposed second matrix with each row of the first matrix. αdistl applies distl to each such pair, resulting in a sequence of sequences of pairs of rows. ααIP applies IP (inner product) to each such pair, thus producing the desired matrix product.

Note ony functions are mentioned, never the data items (variables or constants) to which they are applied. (There was a combining form for creating a constant-valued function from a data value.) This later became known as point-free style. Backus felt it contributed greatly to the power and simplicity of FP.

One of the problems with conventional languages cited by Backus was their complexity and the resultant difficulty in specifying them and proving properties about them. In contrast, Backus exhibited an algebra of programs for FP that could be used for showing program equivalance, for example when transforming a program to a more efficient form. The algebra was based on identities stemming from the properties of the combining forms, for example:

[f1, ..., fN] ○ g ≡ [f1 ○ g, ... fN ○ g]

αf ○ [g1, ..., gN] ≡ [f ○ g1, ..., f ○ gN]

/f ○ [g1, g2, ... gN-1, gN] ≡ f ○ [g1, f ○ [g2, ... f ○ [gN-1, gN]...] ]

/ takes a function on pairs and produces a function on sequences, like APL's reduction operator.

There were also theorems based on these laws for more complex transformations, such as for converting a self-referencing definition into an (infinite) conditional. The paper spent many pages explaining and proving several of these theorems. Examples showed the equivalence between recursive and non-recursive versions of matrix multiplication and factorial.

Finally, Backus presented Applicative State Transition systems, in which the system has a state consisting of a set of named cells each containing a user-defined function or a data item. The user submits a series of inputs, each of which is examined by a system function that dispatches to the appropriate handler, which runs a computation and then produces a pair (output, new state). The system function does a validity check on the new state, then installs it and sends the output to the user. The paper describes this in some detail, including bootstrapping from an empty state, and suggests various ways the system could be elaborated.

Reaction to the paper

Given the prestige of the Turing Award and the provocative title, many people read and discussed the paper. Personal letters from Dana Scott and Robin Milner congratulated Backus in his effort to bring proofs of programs to working programmers, but pointed out a number of technical problems with FP and FFP and encouraged him to base his work on an extended typed λ-calculus such as presented in [Scott1976]. (Scott also chided, "Thank you very much indeed for the several kind references to me. Of course, just as you use the name 'von Neumann' in a generic sense, so you use 'Scott'. I would have suggested including references to my Turing lecture [Scott1977] and to the SIAM paper [Scott1976] where some of the other contributors arc mentioned.") [Scott1978a, b] [Milner1978a, b] ***** Add these plus Backus-Letter_to_Dana_Scott-1978_09_14.pdf to References, part 1.

A more energetic interchange was launched when Edsger Dijkstra reviewed Backus's lecture as number 692 in his personal EWD series, which was directly distributed to about a dozen of Dijkstra's friends but made its way indirectly to a larger audience, including Backus. Its conclusion was relatively bland [Dijkstra1978b]:

"In short, the article is a progress report on a valid research effort but suffers badly from aggressive overselling of its significance, long before convincing results have been reached. This is the more regrettable as it has been published by way of Turing Award Lecture."

but the full review was quite negative, and triggered an exchange of letters between Backus and Dijkstra [Chin2016] in which Dijkstra declared his review had been a "political pamphlet" aimed to counter what he apparently felt was Backus's attack on the axiomatic semantics being developed by Dijkstra, Hoare, and others.

By 2026, the ACM's Digital Library recorded over 2000 citations of [Backus1978b], with more trickling in. Although the vast majority seemed to cite the paper as a reference for "von Neumann architecture", many dozen papers, especially in the first decade, were genuine attempts to apply or extend Backus's ideas in a variety of ways:

  • Extending the algorithm of programs: Banerjee, ...
  • Optimizing transformations: Bellegarde, Norman, ...
  • Implementations: Baden, Choppy et al., Robinson, Biagionni, Valencia, Deleuze.
  • Parallel computation: Ben-Asher et al., Christopher and Ameiss
  • Database querying: Bossi and Ghezzi, Buneman and Frankel
  • Stream processing: Ida and Tanaka, Sheeran, Shultis, Thomas and Stanat
  • Lazy evaluation: Dosch and Möller, Radensky
  • VLSI design: Sheeran, Tsanakas et al.
  • Data flow machines: Zhang et al.
  • and many more -- see References, part 2

Motivating and refining the algebra

Backus had worked alone since I moved to the System R project in 1975. In July 1978 he was joined by John Hayden Williams. Williams received his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a dissertation entitled Bounded Context Parsable Grammars. He joined the faculty at Cornell University, where he conducted research on programming languages. At some point he met John Backus, who mentioned him in the acknowledgements to [Backus1973a] and [Backus1978b]. Perhaps the idea of joining IBM was discussed in December 1977, when Backus gave a talk at Cornell [Backus2003, item 159].

Backus and Williams set to work to improve the algebra of programs. That summer Williams was one of the lecturers at the annual NATO Summer School at Marktoberdorf, Germany. Dijkstra reported [Dijkstra1978a]:

"The last lecture of the last day --on Reduction Languages-- was given by one of the participants, John H. Williams (in the process of moving from Cornell University to IBM? San Jose). It was a brilliant lecture, forcefully delivered. In view of the fact that the participants were the best part of the Summer School, we couldn't have wished for a more appropriate closing lecture."

In August 1979 Backus presented a draft paper at the Summer Workshop on Programming Methodology at UC Santa Cruz [Backus1979]. As with his Turing Award Lecture, he spent many pages comparing his functional approach to a "von Neumann language". His approach was to focus on formal semantics. In an imperative language with statements, assignments, and side-effects, the meaning of a statement (or expression with side-effects) must be modeled as a function mapping stores (memory states) to stores, whereas a functional program is a function mapping values (inputs) to values (outputs). Although he assured the reader he wasn't setting up a "straw man", his informal description of denotational semantics for imperative languages was written in an acerbic style. He concluded that a functional program, using four main combining forms (constant, composition, condition, and construction) was much more powerful because of the existence of the algebra of programs interrelating these combining forms. Of course imperative languages have analogs of these combining forms: constants, compound expressions and semicolon for sequencing statements, conditional expressions and statements, and local variables, but admittedly proofs of correctness and equivalence for imperative languages typically require full predicate logic rather than the equational style advocated by Backus. To be fair, Backus pointed out two problems preventing adoption of functional style: "naming" (variables are useful when lots of quantities need to be kept track of) and "forgetting" (simulating variables with functions brings in stores). The second part of the paper further developed the "linear expansion theorem" of his Turing Award lecture.

Implementations by others

Scott Baden's Berkeley FP was an interpreter written in Franz Lisp and was distributed with several releases of Berkeley Unix; see [BadenPatel198x], [Baden1983a–c].

Arch Robinson's Illinois FP was also an interpreter written in C; it was distributed via the USENET news group comp.sources.unix. See [Robinson1987a–e].

Edoardo S. Biagioni's FPC was written in C; it translated FP to C, which was then compiled with a C compiler; version 1.0 was distributed via the USENET news group comp.sources.unix. See [Biagioni1988].

Andy Valencia's Stanford FP was an interpreter written in C and distributed via the USENET news group comp.sources.unix. See [Valencia1986].

Christophe Deleuze's oc-FP was an interpreter written in OCaml and is distributed via the Deleuze's web site. See [Deleuze2003].

content_text: History of John Backus's functional programming project ***** Work in progress ***** Paul McJones paul@mcjones.org https://mcjones.org/dustydecks Hacker News discussion: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49038035 Last modified 27 July 2026 Abstracts John Backus explored a sequence of applicative, functional and function-level languages starting before 1969 and continuing until he retired in 1991. The goal of this project is to preserve the surviving materials from this research and to put them into context. Comments, suggestions, and donations of additional materials are greatly appreciated. Contents Acknowledgements The software crisis Launching a project Another assistant The Turing Lecture Refining the algebra The FL team Implementations by others Assessment References Related resources Acknowledgements John Backus for hiring me in 1974 and giving me a number of historic materials in 2004. Scott Baden for a copy of [Baden1983b]. Edoardo S. Biagioni for the source code to his FPC and information about Gyula A. Magó's FFP Machine project. Dines Bjørner for information on his work with John Backus. Will Partain for information about Gyula A. Magó. Barry Rosen for permission to post [Rosen1974a, b]. The software crisis In the late 1960s the "software crisis" became a frequent topic of discussion. Computers had become much more capable in speed and memory sizes and prices had come down, but as ambitions grew, a number of programming projects suffered from cost and shedule overruns and poor reliability. A pair of NATO-sponsored conferences on Software Engineering in 1968 and 1969 brought attention to the problems and served as an initial forum for discussing solutions, which included formal methods, design methodologies, and management techniques. Although John Backus attended neither of these conferences, they resonated with his long-held desire to simplify the task of programming. He'd had early success with his Speedcoding and FORTRAN projects. FORTRAN in particular revolutionized the task of writing numerically-oriented programs, in many cases allowing scientists and engineers to write programs rivalling or exceeding the performance of programs written by professional programmers—members of the "priesthood," as Backus sometimes referred to them. After FORTRAN, he participated in the Algol project, and in 1963 was named an IBM Fellow in 1963, giving him the flexibility to choose any problem to work on. He then spent a number of years working on four color conjecture (now theorem). But somewhere around 1967–1969, Backus decided to take another try at the programming problem: "I was just trying to think of some sort of really higher level programming that wasn’t as difficult as Fortran. The problem was that the idea of functional programming, the 'combining forms' and stuff like that, came pretty easily. But trying to make it into a real full system where you could deal with all the other issues that you couldn’t express in that language got very confusing and messy." [Booch2007] Launching a project For several years, Backus worked mostly alone on this new idea. Ted Codd consulted with him briefly, but that didn't last [Booch2007]. In late 1969, Dines Bjørner began working with him, first explaining the details of lambda-calculus and Curry's Combinatory Logic, then writing an interpreter (in PL/I) based on “finite state tree-transformer” semantic for Backus's language (which was then called RedSys) [Bjørner2025, 1972]. Bjørner worked with Backus until 1972, when they parted ways; Bjørner went on to work with Ted Codd [Bjørner2025], [BjørnerEtAl1973]. Backus's first publication was a 1972 research report titled "Reduction languages and variable-free programming"; the report acknowledges Bjørner "for writing a program to reduce Red items which was used to test some of the operators in this paper."[Backus1972a] This report introduced a family of expression-oriented languages with semantics given by simple rewrite rules. The featured language, called Red for reduction, was similiar in size to Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960], but rather than defining a function by describing its effect on the formal parameters, the programmer built up a function from a set of base functions using a function composition operator as well as a set of combining forms (here known as 'modifiers'). Each function took one (implicit) argument, which could be a sequence. This led to a programming style somewhat reminiscent of APL's "one-liners", and Backus later cited APL as an inspiration. During 1972, Phil Summers (then probably a graduate student intern from Yale, later an IBM researcher) did an experimental implementation of Red in Lisp [Summers1972]. This first report was fairly mild in its claims about Red, which he positioned more as a formal system than a practical programming language. In 1973 he followed up with a paper,presented at the first ACM Principles of Programming Languages conference [Backus1973a, c]. It refined the hierarchy of languages, presented a tidied-up version of Red as the centerpiece and concluded: "Hopefully, this work will lead to a semantic theory for a new class of programming languages, one which possesses an axiomatic foundation of the simplicity required for rigorous mathematical treatment." During 1973, Backus went on the lecture circuit, giving 14 lectures at universities and research labs across the country [Backus1973d]. His annual report as an IBM Fellow described that year's work on language frameworks and the Red language, and then made two claims [Backus1974a]: "Simple, whole-entity programming languages, as contrasted to conventional complex, word-at-a-time programming languages, have the potential for drastically reducing the cost of programming. Present efforts to clean up and extend conventional concepts of programming languages have no such potential; ... indeed they will continue to add complexity to languages without dealing with the word-at-a-time problem, as they have for the past 15 years, and thereby actually increase the cost of programming and the expertise required for its practice. (Thus PL/I is perhaps 10 times as complex as Fortran, less economical in execution, and only 20-30% more powerful in expressiveness.)" He concluded, "If there is any truth to the two assertions above, then Research should ask itself whether it has fallen into a comfortable but mistaken orthodoxy with respect to programming languages. I believe it should re-evaluate its emphasis and goals in computer science and programming; at least IBM computer scientists should be aware that reducing the cost of programming would do more to help IBM's growth than perhaps any other technical, accomplishment." In support of these claims, he introduced the phrase "von Neumann bottleneck"—the word-at-a-time nature of conventional computers—and argued that this carried over to the design of conventional programming languages, leading to their inefficiency and complexity. It fell to Patricia Goldberg, Manager of the Automatic Programming group at IBM's Watson Research Center, to respond to Backus [Goldberg1974]. She agreed with the criticality of reducing the cost of programming, the need to go beyond languages of the "PL/I genre," the significance of APL, and the importance of discovering aggregate operations in various fields. But she noted, "I am not, however, convinced that we ought altogether to dispense with the notion of an explicit store and an assignment operator." She pointed out ongoing work at IBM on non-von Neumann frameworks as well as attempts to integrate these into useful programming systems. Backus responded with a vigorous reiteration of the need for IBM Research to study language frameworks with the goal of defining a very simple framework supporting rich definitions [Backus1974b]. Another assistant Despite the lukewarm response from research management, Backus persevered. In the "Plans for 1974" section of his 1973 annual report, Backus had mentioned, "If time and assistance permit, I hope to begin work on an optimizing interpreter for Red languages." He let it be known he was interested in hiring someone to work with him , and Jim Gray, then at IBM San Jose Research and knowing I was looking for permanent employment, introduced me to Backus. I'd attended one of his lectures at UC Berkeley in 1972 and signed up for his mailing list, so I'd received and at least partially digested his two research reports. I'd also worked on interpreters for Snobol4 and APL. For the next 15 months or so, I worked with Backus to refine the language and to explore implementation ideas, including writing some experimental interpreters in Lisp and Mcg, an ISWIM-like language designed by W. H. Burge [Burge1968]. I gave a short talk to the department shortly after joining [McJones1974b] and wrote a technical report on "A Church-Rosser Property of Closed Application Languages" [McJones1975]. During this time Backus and I explored a series of minor variations on the Red language—see [Backus1974b] through [Backus1975b]. Work on the algebra of programs (first mentioned in [Backus1974a]) and modeling state transformations also begin. Sensing that the language was still in flux and the emphasis was more on formal methods than actual implementation, I eventually moved over to the System R relational database project. ***** Include some of my Red evaluators? During this period several researchers at universities began projects based on Backus's ideas. Klaus Berkling initiated design work at GMD in Germany for a reduction-based machine influenced by [Backus1973c]; it is said the be the first reduction machine actually implemented [Berkling1975], [Kluge1983]. Also Gyula A. Magó at the University of North Carolina initiated the FFPM project [Magó1976]. [Partain1989] describes these and other graph reduction machines. The Turing Lecture John Backus received the 1977 ACM Turing Award "For profound, influential, and lasting contributions to the design of practical high-level programming systems, notably through his work on FORTRAN, and for seminal publication of formal procedures for the specification of programming languages." His award lecture "Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style? A Functional Style and Its Algebra of Programs" was published in the Communications of the ACM, received by all ACM members [Backus1978b]. He argued: "Conventional programming languages are growing ever more enormous, but not stronger. Inherent defects at the most basic level cause them to be both fat and weak: their primitive word-at-a-time style of programming, inherited from their common ancestor—the von Neumann computer, their close coupling of semantics to state transitions, their division of programming into a world of expressions and a world of statements, their inability to effectively use powerful combining forms for building new programs from existing ones, and their lack of useful mathematical properties for reasoning about programs." The alternative he proposed was an "informal" functional programming language FP (with a related "formal" version FFP), an algebra of functional programs, and a framework for applicative state transitions (AST) for modeling history-sensitive systems. FP included a set of primitive functions for working with numbers, atoms, and sequences, as well as a set of combining forms for constructing more complex functions from simpler ones. Here's an example function for matrix multiplication: Def MM ≡ (ααIP) ○ (αdistl) ○ distr ○ [1st, trans ○ 2nd] ○ represents function composition, α applies a function to each element of a sequence, and [,...,] applies a list of functions to a value, producing a sequence of results. MM expects a pair of compatible matrices, each represented as a sequences of rows. Reading from right to left, the function in brackets transposes the second matrix while leaving the first matrix intact. distr pairs a copy of the transposed second matrix with each row of the first matrix. αdistl applies distl to each such pair, resulting in a sequence of sequences of pairs of rows. ααIP applies IP (inner product) to each such pair, thus producing the desired matrix product. Note ony functions are mentioned, never the data items (variables or constants) to which they are applied. (There was a combining form for creating a constant-valued function from a data value.) This later became known as point-free style. Backus felt it contributed greatly to the power and simplicity of FP. One of the problems with conventional languages cited by Backus was their complexity and the resultant difficulty in specifying them and proving properties about them. In contrast, Backus exhibited an algebra of programs for FP that could be used for showing program equivalance, for example when transforming a program to a more efficient form. The algebra was based on identities stemming from the properties of the combining forms, for example: [f1, ..., fN] ○ g ≡ [f1 ○ g, ... fN ○ g] αf ○ [g1, ..., gN] ≡ [f ○ g1, ..., f ○ gN] /f ○ [g1, g2, ... gN-1, gN] ≡ f ○ [g1, f ○ [g2, ... f ○ [gN-1, gN]...] ] / takes a function on pairs and produces a function on sequences, like APL's reduction operator. There were also theorems based on these laws for more complex transformations, such as for converting a self-referencing definition into an (infinite) conditional. The paper spent many pages explaining and proving several of these theorems. Examples showed the equivalence between recursive and non-recursive versions of matrix multiplication and factorial. Finally, Backus presented Applicative State Transition systems, in which the system has a state consisting of a set of named cells each containing a user-defined function or a data item. The user submits a series of inputs, each of which is examined by a system function that dispatches to the appropriate handler, which runs a computation and then produces a pair (output, new state). The system function does a validity check on the new state, then installs it and sends the output to the user. The paper describes this in some detail, including bootstrapping from an empty state, and suggests various ways the system could be elaborated. Reaction to the paper Given the prestige of the Turing Award and the provocative title, many people read and discussed the paper. Personal letters from Dana Scott and Robin Milner congratulated Backus in his effort to bring proofs of programs to working programmers, but pointed out a number of technical problems with FP and FFP and encouraged him to base his work on an extended typed λ-calculus such as presented in [Scott1976]. (Scott also chided, "Thank you very much indeed for the several kind references to me. Of course, just as you use the name 'von Neumann' in a generic sense, so you use 'Scott'. I would have suggested including references to my Turing lecture [Scott1977] and to the SIAM paper [Scott1976] where some of the other contributors arc mentioned.") [Scott1978a, b] [Milner1978a, b] ***** Add these plus Backus-Letter_to_Dana_Scott-1978_09_14.pdf to References, part 1. A more energetic interchange was launched when Edsger Dijkstra reviewed Backus's lecture as number 692 in his personal EWD series, which was directly distributed to about a dozen of Dijkstra's friends but made its way indirectly to a larger audience, including Backus. Its conclusion was relatively bland [Dijkstra1978b]: "In short, the article is a progress report on a valid research effort but suffers badly from aggressive overselling of its significance, long before convincing results have been reached. This is the more regrettable as it has been published by way of Turing Award Lecture." but the full review was quite negative, and triggered an exchange of letters between Backus and Dijkstra [Chin2016] in which Dijkstra declared his review had been a "political pamphlet" aimed to counter what he apparently felt was Backus's attack on the axiomatic semantics being developed by Dijkstra, Hoare, and others. By 2026, the ACM's Digital Library recorded over 2000 citations of [Backus1978b], with more trickling in. Although the vast majority seemed to cite the paper as a reference for "von Neumann architecture", many dozen papers, especially in the first decade, were genuine attempts to apply or extend Backus's ideas in a variety of ways: Extending the algorithm of programs: Banerjee, ... Optimizing transformations: Bellegarde, Norman, ... Implementations: Baden, Choppy et al., Robinson, Biagionni, Valencia, Deleuze. Parallel computation: Ben-Asher et al., Christopher and Ameiss Database querying: Bossi and Ghezzi, Buneman and Frankel Stream processing: Ida and Tanaka, Sheeran, Shultis, Thomas and Stanat Lazy evaluation: Dosch and Möller, Radensky VLSI design: Sheeran, Tsanakas et al. Data flow machines: Zhang et al. and many more -- see References, part 2 Motivating and refining the algebra Backus had worked alone since I moved to the System R project in 1975. In July 1978 he was joined by John Hayden Williams. Williams received his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a dissertation entitled Bounded Context Parsable Grammars. He joined the faculty at Cornell University, where he conducted research on programming languages. At some point he met John Backus, who mentioned him in the acknowledgements to [Backus1973a] and [Backus1978b]. Perhaps the idea of joining IBM was discussed in December 1977, when Backus gave a talk at Cornell [Backus2003, item 159]. Backus and Williams set to work to improve the algebra of programs. That summer Williams was one of the lecturers at the annual NATO Summer School at Marktoberdorf, Germany. Dijkstra reported [Dijkstra1978a]: "The last lecture of the last day --on Reduction Languages-- was given by one of the participants, John H. Williams (in the process of moving from Cornell University to IBM? San Jose). It was a brilliant lecture, forcefully delivered. In view of the fact that the participants were the best part of the Summer School, we couldn't have wished for a more appropriate closing lecture." In August 1979 Backus presented a draft paper at the Summer Workshop on Programming Methodology at UC Santa Cruz [Backus1979]. As with his Turing Award Lecture, he spent many pages comparing his functional approach to a "von Neumann language". His approach was to focus on formal semantics. In an imperative language with statements, assignments, and side-effects, the meaning of a statement (or expression with side-effects) must be modeled as a function mapping stores (memory states) to stores, whereas a functional program is a function mapping values (inputs) to values (outputs). Although he assured the reader he wasn't setting up a "straw man", his informal description of denotational semantics for imperative languages was written in an acerbic style. He concluded that a functional program, using four main combining forms (constant, composition, condition, and construction) was much more powerful because of the existence of the algebra of programs interrelating these combining forms. Of course imperative languages have analogs of these combining forms: constants, compound expressions and semicolon for sequencing statements, conditional expressions and statements, and local variables, but admittedly proofs of correctness and equivalence for imperative languages typically require full predicate logic rather than the equational style advocated by Backus. To be fair, Backus pointed out two problems preventing adoption of functional style: "naming" (variables are useful when lots of quantities need to be kept track of) and "forgetting" (simulating variables with functions brings in stores). The second part of the paper further developed the "linear expansion theorem" of his Turing Award lecture. blocks.html_en: In the late 1960s the "software crisis" became a frequent topic of discussion. Computers had become much more capable in speed and memory sizes and prices had come down, but as ambitions grew, a number of programming projects suffered from cost and shedule overruns and poor reliability. A pair of NATO-sponsored conferences on Software Engineering in 1968 and 1969 brought attention to the problems and served as an initial forum for discussing solutions, which included formal methods, design methodologies, and management techniques.

sentences.en: In the late 1960s the "software crisis" became a frequent topic of discussion.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 60 年代末，“软件危机”成为人们频繁讨论的话题。

sentences.en: Computers had become much more capable in speed and memory sizes and prices had come down, but as ambitions grew, a number of programming projects suffered from cost and shedule overruns and poor reliability.
sentences.zh: 计算机在速度和内存大小方面变得更加强大，而且价格也有所下降，但随着野心的增长，许多编程项目都遭受了成本和工期超支以及可靠性差的困扰。

sentences.en: A pair of NATO-sponsored conferences on Software Engineering in 1968 and 1969 brought attention to the problems and served as an initial forum for discussing solutions, which included formal methods, design methodologies, and management techniques.
sentences.zh: 1968 年和 1969 年北约主办的两次软件工程会议引起了人们对这些问题的关注，并成为讨论解决方案的初始论坛，其中包括形式方法、设计方法和管理技术。

blocks.html_en: Although John Backus attended neither of these conferences, they resonated with his long-held desire to simplify the task of programming. He'd had early success with his Speedcoding and FORTRAN projects. FORTRAN in particular revolutionized the task of writing numerically-oriented programs, in many cases allowing scientists and engineers to write programs rivalling or exceeding the performance of programs written by professional programmers—members of the "priesthood," as Backus sometimes referred to them. After FORTRAN, he participated in the Algol project, and in 1963 was named an IBM Fellow in 1963, giving him the flexibility to choose any problem to work on. He then spent a number of years working on four color conjecture (now theorem). But somewhere around 1967–1969, Backus decided to take another try at the programming problem:

sentences.en: Although John Backus attended neither of these conferences, they resonated with his long-held desire to simplify the task of programming.
sentences.zh: 尽管约翰·巴克斯（John Backus）没有参加这两次会议，但这些会议与他长期以来简化编程任务的愿望产生了共鸣。

sentences.en: He'd had early success with his Speedcoding and FORTRAN projects.
sentences.zh: 他的 Speedcoding 和 FORTRAN 项目已经取得了早期的成功。

sentences.en: FORTRAN in particular revolutionized the task of writing numerically-oriented programs, in many cases allowing scientists and engineers to write programs rivalling or exceeding the performance of programs written by professional programmers—members of the "priesthood," as Backus sometimes referred to them.
sentences.zh: FORTRAN 尤其彻底地改变了编写面向数字的程序的任务，在许多情况下允许科学家和工程师编写的程序可以与专业程序员（巴克斯有时称他们为“神职人员”的成员）编写的程序相媲美或超过其性能。

sentences.en: After FORTRAN, he participated in the Algol project, and in 1963 was named an IBM Fellow in 1963, giving him the flexibility to choose any problem to work on.
sentences.zh: 在 FORTRAN 之后，他参与了 Algol 项目，并于 1963 年被任命为 IBM 院士，这使他能够灵活地选择要解决的任何问题。

sentences.en: He then spent a number of years working on four color conjecture (now theorem).
sentences.zh: 然后，他花了几年时间研究四色猜想（现在的定理）。

sentences.en: But somewhere around 1967–1969, Backus decided to take another try at the programming problem:
sentences.zh: 但在 1967 年至 1969 年间，巴克斯决定再次尝试解决编程问题：

blocks.html_en: "I was just trying to think of some sort of really higher level programming that wasn’t as difficult as Fortran. The problem was that the idea of functional programming, the 'combining forms' and stuff like that, came pretty easily. But trying to make it into a real full system where you could deal with all the other issues that you couldn’t express in that language got very confusing and messy." [Booch2007]

sentences.en: "I was just trying to think of some sort of really higher level programming that wasn’t as difficult as Fortran.
sentences.zh: “我只是想尝试某种真正更高级别的编程，而且不像 Fortran 那样困难。

sentences.en: The problem was that the idea of functional programming, the 'combining forms' and stuff like that, came pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 问题是函数式编程的思想、“组合形式”和类似的东西来得很容易。

sentences.en: But trying to make it into a real full system where you could deal with all the other issues that you couldn’t express in that language got very confusing and messy." [Booch2007]
sentences.zh: 但试图将其变成一个真正完整的系统，在其中可以处理所有其他无法用该语言表达的问题，这会变得非常混乱和混乱。” [Booch2007]

blocks.html_en: For several years, Backus worked mostly alone on this new idea. Ted Codd consulted with him briefly, but that didn't last [Booch2007]. In late 1969, Dines Bjørner began working with him, first explaining the details of lambda-calculus and Curry's Combinatory Logic, then writing an interpreter (in PL/I) based on “finite state tree-transformer” semantic for Backus's language (which was then called RedSys) [Bjørner2025, 1972]. Bjørner worked with Backus until 1972, when they parted ways; Bjørner went on to work with Ted Codd [Bjørner2025], [BjørnerEtAl1973].

sentences.en: For several years, Backus worked mostly alone on this new idea.
sentences.zh: 几年来，巴克斯大部分时间都是独自研究这个新想法。

sentences.en: Ted Codd consulted with him briefly, but that didn't last [Booch2007].
sentences.zh: Ted Codd 与他进行了短暂的协商，但这并没有持续多久[Booch2007]。

sentences.en: In late 1969, Dines Bjørner began working with him, first explaining the details of lambda-calculus and Curry's Combinatory Logic, then writing an interpreter (in PL/I) based on “finite state tree-transformer” semantic for Backus's language (which was then called RedSys) [Bjørner2025, 1972].
sentences.zh: 1969 年底，Dines Bjørner 开始与他合作，首先解释 lambda 演算和 Curry 组合逻辑的细节，然后为 Backus 语言（当时称为 RedSys）编写一个基于“有限状态树变换器”语义的解释器（在 PL/I 中）[Bjørner2025, 1972]。

sentences.en: Bjørner worked with Backus until 1972, when they parted ways; Bjørner went on to work with Ted Codd [Bjørner2025], [BjørnerEtAl1973].
sentences.zh: 比约纳 (Bjørner) 与巴科斯 (Backus) 一直合作到 1972 年，之后他们分道扬镳。 Bjørner 继续与 Ted Codd [Bjørner2025]、[BjørnerEtAl1973] 合作。

blocks.html_en: Backus's first publication was a 1972 research report titled "Reduction languages and variable-free programming"; the report acknowledges Bjørner "for writing a program to reduce Red items which was used to test some of the operators in this paper."[Backus1972a] This report introduced a family of expression-oriented languages with semantics given by simple rewrite rules. The featured language, called Red for reduction, was similiar in size to Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960], but rather than defining a function by describing its effect on the formal parameters, the programmer built up a function from a set of base functions using a function composition operator as well as a set of combining forms (here known as 'modifiers'). Each function took one (implicit) argument, which could be a sequence. This led to a programming style somewhat reminiscent of APL's "one-liners", and Backus later cited APL as an inspiration. During 1972, Phil Summers (then probably a graduate student intern from Yale, later an IBM researcher) did an experimental implementation of Red in Lisp [Summers1972].

sentences.en: Backus's first publication was a 1972 research report titled "Reduction languages and variable-free programming"; the report acknowledges Bjørner "for writing a program to reduce Red items which was used to test some of the operators in this paper."[Backus1972a] This report introduced a family of expression-oriented languages with semantics given by simple rewrite rules.
sentences.zh: 巴科斯的第一篇出版物是 1972 年的一份研究报告，题为《Reduction languages and Variable-freeprogramming》；该报告承认 Bjørner“编写了一个程序来减少红色项目，该程序用于测试本文中的一些运算符。”[Backus1972a] 该报告介绍了一系列面向表达式的语言，其语义由简单的重写规则给出。

sentences.en: The featured language, called Red for reduction, was similiar in size to Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960], but rather than defining a function by describing its effect on the formal parameters, the programmer built up a function from a set of base functions using a function composition operator as well as a set of combining forms (here known as 'modifiers').
sentences.zh: 这种特色语言称为 Red forduction，其大小与 Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960] 类似，但程序员不是通过描述函数对形式参数的影响来定义函数，而是使用函数组合运算符以及一组组合形式（此处称为“修饰符”）从一组基本函数构建函数。

sentences.en: Each function took one (implicit) argument, which could be a sequence.
sentences.zh: 每个函数都采用一个（隐式）参数，该参数可以是一个序列。

sentences.en: This led to a programming style somewhat reminiscent of APL's "one-liners", and Backus later cited APL as an inspiration.
sentences.zh: 这导致了一种有点让人想起 APL 的“俏皮话”的编程风格，巴克斯后来引用了 APL 作为灵感。

sentences.en: During 1972, Phil Summers (then probably a graduate student intern from Yale, later an IBM researcher) did an experimental implementation of Red in Lisp [Summers1972].
sentences.zh: 1972 年，Phil Summers（当时可能是耶鲁大学的研究生实习生，后来成为 IBM 研究员）在 Lisp 中实验性地实现了 Red [Summers1972]。

blocks.html_en: This first report was fairly mild in its claims about Red, which he positioned more as a formal system than a practical programming language. In 1973 he followed up with a paper,presented at the first ACM Principles of Programming Languages conference [Backus1973a, c]. It refined the hierarchy of languages, presented a tidied-up version of Red as the centerpiece and concluded: "Hopefully, this work will lead to a semantic theory for a new class of programming languages, one which possesses an axiomatic foundation of the simplicity required for rigorous mathematical treatment."

sentences.en: This first report was fairly mild in its claims about Red, which he positioned more as a formal system than a practical programming language.
sentences.zh: 第一份报告对 Red 的描述相当温和，他将 Red 定位为一种正式的系统，而不是一种实用的编程语言。

sentences.en: In 1973 he followed up with a paper,presented at the first ACM Principles of Programming Languages conference [Backus1973a, c].
sentences.zh: 1973 年，他在第一届 ACM 编程语言原理会议上发表了一篇论文 [Backus1973a, c]。

sentences.en: It refined the hierarchy of languages, presented a tidied-up version of Red as the centerpiece and concluded: "Hopefully, this work will lead to a semantic theory for a new class of programming languages, one which possesses an axiomatic foundation of the simplicity required for rigorous mathematical treatment."
sentences.zh: 它完善了语言的层次结构，提出了 Red 的整理版本作为核心，并得出结论：“希望这项工作将为一类新的编程语言带来语义理论，该语言拥有严格数学处理所需的简单性的公理基础。”

blocks.html_en: During 1973, Backus went on the lecture circuit, giving 14 lectures at universities and research labs across the country [Backus1973d]. His annual report as an IBM Fellow described that year's work on language frameworks and the Red language, and then made two claims [Backus1974a]:

sentences.en: During 1973, Backus went on the lecture circuit, giving 14 lectures at universities and research labs across the country [Backus1973d].
sentences.zh: 1973 年，巴克斯进行巡回演讲，在全国各地的大学和研究实验室进行了 14 场演讲 [Backus1973d]。

sentences.en: His annual report as an IBM Fellow described that year's work on language frameworks and the Red language, and then made two claims [Backus1974a]:
sentences.zh: 他作为 IBM Fellow 的年度报告描述了当年在语言框架和 Red 语言方面的工作，然后提出了两个主张 [Backus1974a]：

blocks.html_en: • "Simple, whole-entity programming languages, as contrasted to conventional complex, word-at-a-time programming languages, have the potential for drastically reducing the cost of programming.

sentences.en: "Simple, whole-entity programming languages, as contrasted to conventional complex, word-at-a-time programming languages, have the potential for drastically reducing the cost of programming.
sentences.zh: “与传统的复杂的、一次一个字的编程语言相比，简单的、整体的编程语言有可能大幅降低编程成本。

blocks.html_en: • Present efforts to clean up and extend conventional concepts of programming languages have no such potential; ... indeed they will continue to add complexity to languages without dealing with the word-at-a-time problem, as they have for the past 15 years, and thereby actually increase the cost of programming and the expertise required for its practice. (Thus PL/I is perhaps 10 times as complex as Fortran, less economical in execution, and only 20-30% more powerful in expressiveness.)"

sentences.en: Present efforts to clean up and extend conventional concepts of programming languages have no such potential; ...
sentences.zh: 目前清理和扩展编程语言传统概念的努力还没有这样的潜力。 ...

sentences.en: indeed they will continue to add complexity to languages without dealing with the word-at-a-time problem, as they have for the past 15 years, and thereby actually increase the cost of programming and the expertise required for its practice.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们将继续增加语言的复杂性，而不像过去 15 年那样处理一次单词的问题，从而实际上增加了编程成本和实践所需的专业知识。

sentences.en: (Thus PL/I is perhaps 10 times as complex as Fortran, less economical in execution, and only 20-30% more powerful in expressiveness.)"
sentences.zh: （因此 PL/I 的复杂度可能是 Fortran 的 10 倍，执行起来更不经济，但表达能力只比 Fortran 强 20-30%。）

blocks.html_en: He concluded, "If there is any truth to the two assertions above, then Research should ask itself whether it has fallen into a comfortable but mistaken orthodoxy with respect to programming languages. I believe it should re-evaluate its emphasis and goals in computer science and programming; at least IBM computer scientists should be aware that reducing the cost of programming would do more to help IBM's growth than perhaps any other technical, accomplishment." In support of these claims, he introduced the phrase "von Neumann bottleneck"—the word-at-a-time nature of conventional computers—and argued that this carried over to the design of conventional programming languages, leading to their inefficiency and complexity.

sentences.en: He concluded, "If there is any truth to the two assertions above, then Research should ask itself whether it has fallen into a comfortable but mistaken orthodoxy with respect to programming languages.
sentences.zh: 他总结道：“如果上述两个断言有任何道理，那么 Research 应该扪心自问，在编程语言方面，它是否已经陷入了一种舒适但错误的正统观念。

sentences.en: I believe it should re-evaluate its emphasis and goals in computer science and programming; at least IBM computer scientists should be aware that reducing the cost of programming would do more to help IBM's growth than perhaps any other technical, accomplishment."
sentences.zh: 我认为它应该重新评估其在计算机科学和编程方面的重点和目标；至少 IBM 计算机科学家应该意识到，降低编程成本可能比任何其他技术成就更能帮助 IBM 发展。”

sentences.en: In support of these claims, he introduced the phrase "von Neumann bottleneck"—the word-at-a-time nature of conventional computers—and argued that this carried over to the design of conventional programming languages, leading to their inefficiency and complexity.
sentences.zh: 为了支持这些主张，他引入了“冯·诺依曼瓶颈”一词（传统计算机的一次单词性质），并认为这会延续到传统编程语言的设计中，导致其低效率和复杂性。

blocks.html_en: It fell to Patricia Goldberg, Manager of the Automatic Programming group at IBM's Watson Research Center, to respond to Backus [Goldberg1974]. She agreed with the criticality of reducing the cost of programming, the need to go beyond languages of the "PL/I genre," the significance of APL, and the importance of discovering aggregate operations in various fields. But she noted, "I am not, however, convinced that we ought altogether to dispense with the notion of an explicit store and an assignment operator." She pointed out ongoing work at IBM on non-von Neumann frameworks as well as attempts to integrate these into useful programming systems. Backus responded with a vigorous reiteration of the need for IBM Research to study language frameworks with the goal of defining a very simple framework supporting rich definitions [Backus1974b].

sentences.en: It fell to Patricia Goldberg, Manager of the Automatic Programming group at IBM's Watson Research Center, to respond to Backus [Goldberg1974].
sentences.zh: IBM 沃森研究中心自动编程小组的经理 Patricia Goldberg 负责对 Backus 做出回应 [Goldberg1974]。

sentences.en: She agreed with the criticality of reducing the cost of programming, the need to go beyond languages of the "PL/I genre," the significance of APL, and the importance of discovering aggregate operations in various fields.
sentences.zh: 她同意降低编程成本的重要性、超越“PL/I 流派”语言的必要性、APL 的重要性以及发现各个领域聚合操作的重要性。

sentences.en: But she noted, "I am not, however, convinced that we ought altogether to dispense with the notion of an explicit store and an assignment operator."
sentences.zh: 但她指出，“然而，我并不相信我们应该完全放弃显式存储和赋值运算符的概念。”

sentences.en: She pointed out ongoing work at IBM on non-von Neumann frameworks as well as attempts to integrate these into useful programming systems.
sentences.zh: 她指出了 IBM 正在进行的非冯诺依曼框架的工作以及将这些框架集成到有用的编程系统中的尝试。

sentences.en: Backus responded with a vigorous reiteration of the need for IBM Research to study language frameworks with the goal of defining a very simple framework supporting rich definitions [Backus1974b].
sentences.zh: Backus 对此作出回应，强烈重申 IBM 研究中心需要研究语言框架，其目标是定义一个支持丰富定义的非常简单的框架 [Backus1974b]。

blocks.html_en: Despite the lukewarm response from research management, Backus persevered. In the "Plans for 1974" section of his 1973 annual report, Backus had mentioned, "If time and assistance permit, I hope to begin work on an optimizing interpreter for Red languages." He let it be known he was interested in hiring someone to work with him , and Jim Gray, then at IBM San Jose Research and knowing I was looking for permanent employment, introduced me to Backus. I'd attended one of his lectures at UC Berkeley in 1972 and signed up for his mailing list, so I'd received and at least partially digested his two research reports. I'd also worked on interpreters for Snobol4 and APL. For the next 15 months or so, I worked with Backus to refine the language and to explore implementation ideas, including writing some experimental interpreters in Lisp and Mcg, an ISWIM-like language designed by W. H. Burge [Burge1968]. I gave a short talk to the department shortly after joining [McJones1974b] and wrote a technical report on "A Church-Rosser Property of Closed Application Languages" [McJones1975]. During this time Backus and I explored a series of minor variations on the Red language—see [Backus1974b] through [Backus1975b]. Work on the algebra of programs (first mentioned in [Backus1974a]) and modeling state transformations also begin. Sensing that the language was still in flux and the emphasis was more on formal methods than actual implementation, I eventually moved over to the System R relational database project.

sentences.en: Despite the lukewarm response from research management, Backus persevered.
sentences.zh: 尽管研究管理层反应冷淡，巴克斯还是坚持了下来。

blocks.html_en: "Conventional programming languages are growing ever more enormous, but not stronger. Inherent defects at the most basic level cause them to be both fat and weak: their primitive word-at-a-time style of programming, inherited from their common ancestor—the von Neumann computer, their close coupling of semantics to state transitions, their division of programming into a world of expressions and a world of statements, their inability to effectively use powerful combining forms for building new programs from existing ones, and their lack of useful mathematical properties for reasoning about programs."

blocks.html_en: Finally, Backus presented Applicative State Transition systems, in which the system has a state consisting of a set of named cells each containing a user-defined function or a data item. The user submits a series of inputs, each of which is examined by a system function that dispatches to the appropriate handler, which runs a computation and then produces a pair (output, new state). The system function does a validity check on the new state, then installs it and sends the output to the user. The paper describes this in some detail, including bootstrapping from an empty state, and suggests various ways the system could be elaborated.

blocks.html_en: Given the prestige of the Turing Award and the provocative title, many people read and discussed the paper. (Scott also chided, "Thank you very much indeed for the several kind references to me. Of course, just as you use the name 'von Neumann' in a generic sense, so you use 'Scott'. I would have suggested including references to my Turing lecture [Scott1977] and to the SIAM paper [Scott1976] where some of the other contributors arc mentioned.") blocks.html_en: Motivating and refining the algebra

Backus had worked alone since I moved to the System R project in 1975. In July 1978 he was joined by John Hayden Williams. Williams received his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison with a dissertation entitled Bounded Context Parsable Grammars. He joined the faculty at Cornell University, where he conducted research on programming languages. At some point he met John Backus, who mentioned him in the acknowledgements to [Backus1973a] and [Backus1978b]. Perhaps the idea of joining IBM was discussed in December 1977, when Backus gave a talk at Cornell [Backus2003, item 159].

blocks.html_en: In August 1979 Backus presented a draft paper at the Summer Workshop on Programming Methodology at UC Santa Cruz [Backus1979]. As with his Turing Award Lecture, he spent many pages comparing his functional approach to a "von Neumann language". His approach was to focus on formal semantics. In an imperative language with statements, assignments, and side-effects, the meaning of a statement (or expression with side-effects) must be modeled as a function mapping stores (memory states) to stores, whereas a functional program is a function mapping values (inputs) to values (outputs). Although he assured the reader he wasn't setting up a "straw man", his informal description of denotational semantics for imperative languages was written in an acerbic style. He concluded that a functional program, using four main combining forms (constant, composition, condition, and construction) was much more powerful because of the existence of the algebra of programs interrelating these combining forms. Of course imperative languages have analogs of these combining forms: constants, compound expressions and semicolon for sequencing statements, conditional expressions and statements, and local variables, but admittedly proofs of correctness and equivalence for imperative languages typically require full predicate logic rather than the equational style advocated by Backus. To be fair, Backus pointed out two problems preventing adoption of functional style: "naming" (variables are useful when lots of quantities need to be kept track of) and "forgetting" (simulating variables with functions brings in stores). The second part of the paper further developed the "linear expansion theorem" of his Turing Award lecture.

sentences.zh: 在具有语句、赋值和副作用的命令式语言中，语句（或具有副作用的表达式）的含义必须建模为将存储（内存状态）映射到存储的函数，而函数式程序是将值（输入）映射到值（输出）的函数。

sentences.en: He concluded that a functional program, using four main combining forms (constant, composition, condition, and construction) was much more powerful because of the existence of the algebra of programs interrelating these combining forms.

sentences.en: Of course imperative languages have analogs of these combining forms: constants, compound expressions and semicolon for sequencing statements, conditional expressions and statements, and local variables, but admittedly proofs of correctness and equivalence for imperative languages typically require full predicate logic rather than the equational style advocated by Backus.
sentences.zh: 当然，命令式语言具有这些组合形式的类似物：常量、用于排序语句的复合表达式和分号、条件表达式和语句以及局部变量，但无可否认，命令式语言的正确性和等价性证明通常需要完整的谓词逻辑，而不是巴科斯提倡的等式风格。

sentences.en: To be fair, Backus pointed out two problems preventing adoption of functional style: "naming" (variables are useful when lots of quantities need to be kept track of) and "forgetting" (simulating variables with functions brings in stores).
sentences.zh: 公平地说，巴克斯指出了阻碍采用函数式风格的两个问题：“命名”（当需要跟踪大量数量时，变量很有用）和“遗忘”（用函数模拟变量会带来存储）。

sentences.en: The second part of the paper further developed the "linear expansion theorem" of his Turing Award lecture.
sentences.zh: 论文的第二部分进一步发展了他在图灵奖演讲中的“线性展开定理”。

blocks.html_en: "Informally, FP84 is the result of altering the language FP of [Backus 781 to include infinite sequences, programmer-defined combining forms, and lazy evaluation. Moreover, unlike the formal language FFP of [Backus 781, FP84 makes a clear distinction between objects and functions; i.e., sequences of objects are no longer used to represent functions. These extensions are accomplished in FP84 by removing the FP restriction that sequence construction be applied only to non-l objects; in FP84 the entire set of expressions (including those whose meaning is I) is closed under sequence construction. A complete description of FP84, including an operational and a denotational semantics, may be found in [HWI 853 and [HW2 863."

约翰·巴克斯 (John Backus) 函数式编程项目的历史

***** 工作正在进行中 *****

保罗·麦克琼斯 paul@mcjones.org https://mcjones.org/dustydecks

黑客新闻讨论：https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49038035

最后修改时间：2026 年 7 月 27 日

摘要

John Backus 从 1969 年之前开始探索一系列应用性、函数式和函数级语言，一直持续到 1991 年退休。 该项目的目标是保存本研究中幸存的材料并将其置于背景中。 非常感谢评论、建议和额外材料的捐赠。

内容

  • 致谢
  • 软件危机
  • 启动项目
  • 另一位助理
  • 图灵讲座
  • 精炼代数
  • 佛罗里达队
  • 其他人的实施
  • 评估

致谢

  • 约翰·巴克斯 (John Backus) 在 1974 年聘用了我，并在 2004 年为我提供了许多历史资料。
  • Scott Baden 索取 [Baden1983b] 的副本。
  • 爱德华·S。 Biagioni 获取其 FPC 的源代码以及有关 Gyula A 的信息。 Magó 的 FFP 机器项目。
  • Dines Bjørner 了解有关他与约翰·巴克斯 (John Backus) 合作的信息。
  • Will Parttain 了解有关 Gyula A 的信息。 马戈。
  • 巴里·罗森 (Barry Rosen) 允许发帖 [Rosen1974a, b]。

软件危机

20 世纪 60 年代末，“软件危机”成为人们频繁讨论的话题。 计算机在速度和内存大小方面变得更加强大，而且价格也有所下降，但随着野心的增长，许多编程项目都遭受了成本和工期超支以及可靠性差的困扰。 1968 年和 1969 年北约主办的两次软件工程会议引起了人们对这些问题的关注，并成为讨论解决方案的初始论坛，其中包括形式方法、设计方法和管理技术。

尽管约翰·巴克斯（John Backus）没有参加这两次会议，但这些会议与他长期以来简化编程任务的愿望产生了共鸣。 他的 Speedcoding 和 FORTRAN 项目已经取得了早期的成功。 FORTRAN 尤其彻底地改变了编写面向数字的程序的任务，在许多情况下允许科学家和工程师编写的程序可以与专业程序员（巴克斯有时称他们为“神职人员”的成员）编写的程序相媲美或超过其性能。 在 FORTRAN 之后，他参与了 Algol 项目，并于 1963 年被任命为 IBM 院士，这使他能够灵活地选择要解决的任何问题。 然后，他花了几年时间研究四色猜想（现在的定理）。 但在 1967 年至 1969 年间，巴克斯决定再次尝试解决编程问题：

“我只是想尝试某种真正更高级别的编程，而且不像 Fortran 那样困难。 问题是函数式编程的思想、“组合形式”和类似的东西来得很容易。 但试图将其变成一个真正完整的系统，在其中可以处理所有其他无法用该语言表达的问题，这会变得非常混乱和混乱。” [Booch2007]

启动项目

几年来，巴克斯大部分时间都是独自研究这个新想法。 Ted Codd 与他进行了短暂的协商，但这并没有持续多久[Booch2007]。 1969 年底，Dines Bjørner 开始与他合作，首先解释 lambda 演算和 Curry 组合逻辑的细节，然后为 Backus 语言（当时称为 RedSys）编写一个基于“有限状态树变换器”语义的解释器（在 PL/I 中）[Bjørner2025, 1972]。 比约纳 (Bjørner) 与巴科斯 (Backus) 一直合作到 1972 年，之后他们分道扬镳。 Bjørner 继续与 Ted Codd [Bjørner2025]、[BjørnerEtAl1973] 合作。

巴科斯的第一篇出版物是 1972 年的一份研究报告，题为《Reduction languages and Variable-freeprogramming》；该报告承认 Bjørner“编写了一个程序来减少红色项目，该程序用于测试本文中的一些运算符。”[Backus1972a] 该报告介绍了一系列面向表达式的语言，其语义由简单的重写规则给出。 这种特色语言称为 Red forduction，其大小与 Pure Lisp [McCarthy1960] 类似，但程序员不是通过描述函数对形式参数的影响来定义函数，而是使用函数组合运算符以及一组组合形式（此处称为“修饰符”）从一组基本函数构建函数。 每个函数都采用一个（隐式）参数，该参数可以是一个序列。 这导致了一种有点让人想起 APL 的“俏皮话”的编程风格，巴克斯后来引用了 APL 作为灵感。 1972 年，Phil Summers（当时可能是耶鲁大学的研究生实习生，后来成为 IBM 研究员）在 Lisp 中实验性地实现了 Red [Summers1972]。

第一份报告对 Red 的描述相当温和，他将 Red 定位为一种正式的系统，而不是一种实用的编程语言。 1973 年，他在第一届 ACM 编程语言原理会议上发表了一篇论文 [Backus1973a, c]。 它完善了语言的层次结构，提出了 Red 的整理版本作为核心，并得出结论：“希望这项工作将为一类新的编程语言带来语义理论，该语言拥有严格数学处理所需的简单性的公理基础。”

1973 年，巴克斯进行巡回演讲，在全国各地的大学和研究实验室进行了 14 场演讲 [Backus1973d]。 他作为 IBM Fellow 的年度报告描述了当年在语言框架和 Red 语言方面的工作，然后提出了两个主张 [Backus1974a]：

  1. “与传统的复杂的、一次一个字的编程语言相比，简单的、整体的编程语言有可能大幅降低编程成本。
  2. 目前清理和扩展编程语言传统概念的努力还没有这样的潜力。 ... 事实上，他们将继续增加语言的复杂性，而不像过去 15 年那样处理一次单词的问题，从而实际上增加了编程成本和实践所需的专业知识。 （因此 PL/I 的复杂度可能是 Fortran 的 10 倍，执行起来更不经济，但表达能力只比 Fortran 强 20-30%。）

他总结道：“如果上述两个断言有任何道理，那么 Research 应该扪心自问，在编程语言方面，它是否已经陷入了一种舒适但错误的正统观念。 我认为它应该重新评估其在计算机科学和编程方面的重点和目标；至少 IBM 计算机科学家应该意识到，降低编程成本可能比任何其他技术成就更能帮助 IBM 发展。” 为了支持这些主张，他引入了“冯·诺依曼瓶颈”一词（传统计算机的一次单词性质），并认为这会延续到传统编程语言的设计中，导致其低效率和复杂性。

IBM 沃森研究中心自动编程小组的经理 Patricia Goldberg 负责对 Backus 做出回应 [Goldberg1974]。 她同意降低编程成本的重要性、超越“PL/I 流派”语言的必要性、APL 的重要性以及发现各个领域聚合操作的重要性。 但她指出，“然而，我并不相信我们应该完全放弃显式存储和赋值运算符的概念。” 她指出了 IBM 正在进行的非冯诺依曼框架的工作以及将这些框架集成到有用的编程系统中的尝试。 Backus 对此作出回应，强烈重申 IBM 研究中心需要研究语言框架，其目标是定义一个支持丰富定义的非常简单的框架 [Backus1974b]。

另一位助理

尽管研究管理层反应冷淡，巴克斯还是坚持了下来。 巴克斯在 1973 年年度报告的“1974 年计划”部分中提到，“如果时间和援助允许，我希望开始研究红色语言的优化解释器”。 他表示他有兴趣雇用某人与他一起工作，当时在 IBM 圣何塞研究中心的吉姆·格雷（Jim Gray）知道我正在寻找永久工作，于是将我介绍给了巴科斯。 1972 年，我在加州大学伯克利分校听过他的一场讲座，并注册了他的邮件列表，因此我收到了并至少部分消化了他的两份研究报告。 我还曾为 Snobol4 和 APL 做过口译员。 在接下来的 15 个月左右的时间里，我与 Backus 合作完善该语言并探索实现思路，包括用 Lisp 和 Mcg（一种由 W. H. 伯格[Burge1968]。 加入 [McJones1974b] 后不久，我向该部门进行了一次简短的演讲，并撰写了一份关于“封闭应用语言的 Church-Rosser 属性”[McJones1975] 的技术报告。 在此期间，巴克斯和我探索了 Red 语言的一系列细微变化——请参阅 [Backus1974b] 到 [Backus1975b]。 程序代数（在 [Backus1974a] 中首次提到）和建模状态转换的工作也开始了。 意识到该语言仍在不断变化，并且重点更多地放在形式方法而不是实际实现上，我最终转向了 System R 关系数据库项目。

***** 包括我的一些红色评估者吗？

在此期间，大学的几位研究人员开始了基于巴科斯想法的项目。 Klaus Berkling 在德国 GMD 发起了受 [Backus1973c] 影响的基于减速的机器的设计工作；据说这是第一台实际实施的减速机[Berkling1975]，[Kluge1983]。 还有久拉 A. 北卡罗来纳大学的 Magó 发起了 FFPM 项目 [Magó1976]。 [Parttain1989] 描述了这些和其他图缩减机。

图灵讲座

约翰·巴科斯 (John Backus) 荣获 1977 年 ACM 图灵奖，“表彰他对实用高级编程系统设计的深刻、有影响力和持久的贡献，特别是通过他在 FORTRAN 方面的工作，以及对编程语言规范的正式过程的开创性出版。” 他的获奖演讲《编程能否从冯诺依曼风格中解放出来？ 函数式风格及其程序代数”发表在 ACM Communications 上，所有 ACM 成员均收到 [Backus1978b]。 他辩称：

“传统的编程语言变得越来越庞大，但并没有变得更强大。 最基本层面上的固有缺陷导致它们既肥又弱：它们原始的一次一个字的编程风格，继承自它们的共同祖先——冯·诺依曼计算机，它们的语义与状态转换的紧密耦合，它们将编程划分为表达式世界和语句世界，它们无法有效地使用强大的组合形式从现有程序构建新程序，以及它们缺乏用于推理程序的有用数学属性。

他提出的替代方案是一种“非正式”函数式编程语言 FP（以及相关的“正式”版本 FFP）、函数式程序的代数以及用于对历史敏感系统进行建模的应用状态转换 (AST) 框架。 FP 包括一组用于处理数字、原子和序列的原始函数，以及一组用于从简单函数构造更复杂函数的组合形式。 这是矩阵乘法的示例函数：

Def MM == (ααIP) ○ (αdistl) ○ distr ○ [1st, trans ○ 2nd]

○ 表示函数组合，α 将函数应用于序列的每个元素，[,...,] 将函数列表应用于值，产生结果序列。 MM 期望一对兼容的矩阵，每个矩阵表示为行序列。 从右向左阅读，括号中的函数转置第二个矩阵，同时保持第一个矩阵不变。 distr 将转置后的第二个矩阵的副本与第一个矩阵的每一行配对。 αdistl 将 distl 应用于每个这样的对，从而产生行对序列的序列。 ααIP 将 IP（内积）应用于每个这样的对，从而产生所需的矩阵乘积。

请注意，仅提到了函数，而没有提到它们所应用的数据项（变量或常量）。 （有一种组合形式可以根据数据值创建常值函数。） 这后来被称为无点风格。 Backus 认为它​​对 FP 的强大功能和简单性做出了巨大贡献。

巴科斯引用的传统语言的问题之一是它们的复杂性以及由此导致的指定它们和证明它们的属性的困难。 相比之下，巴科斯展示了 FP 程序的代数，可用于显示程序等价性，例如将程序转换为更有效的形式时。 代数基于源自组合形式的属性的恒等式，例如：

[f1, ..., fN] ○ g ≡ [f1 ○ g, ... fN ○ g]

αf ○ [g1, ..., gN] ≡ [f ○ g1, ..., f ○ gN]

/f ○ [g1, g2, ... gN-1, gN] ≡ f ○ [g1, f ○ [g2, ... f ○ [gN-1, gN]...] ]

/ 接受对上的函数并生成序列上的函数，就像 APL 的归约运算符。

还有基于这些定律的定理，用于更复杂的转换，例如将自引用定义转换为（无限）条件。 这篇论文用了很多页来解释和证明其中的几个定理。 示例显示了矩阵乘法和阶乘的递归和非递归版本之间的等效性。

最后，巴科斯提出了应用状态转换系统，其中系统的状态由一组命名单元组成，每个命名单元包含用户定义的函数或数据项。 用户提交一系列输入，每个输入都由系统函数检查，该系统函数分派到适当的处理程序，该处理程序运行计算，然后生成一对（输出，新状态）。 系统函数对新状态进行有效性检查，然后安装它并将输出发送给用户。 该论文对此进行了一些详细描述，包括从空状态引导，并提出了完善该系统的各种方法。

对论文的反应

鉴于图灵奖的声望和具有挑衅性的标题，许多人阅读并讨论了这篇论文。 Dana Scott 和 Robin Milner 的私人信件祝贺 Backus 为程序员提供程序证明所做的努力，但也指出了 FP 和 FFP 的一些技术问题，并鼓励他将工作建立在扩展类型的 λ 演算的基础上，例如 [Scott1976] 中提出的。 （斯科特还责备道：“确实非常感谢您对我的多次善意提及。 当然，就像您在一般意义上使用“冯·诺依曼”这个名字一样，您也可以使用“斯科特”。 我建议包括对我的图灵讲座 [Scott1977] 和 SIAM 论文 [Scott1976] 的引用，其中提到了其他一些贡献者。") [Scott1978a, b] [Milner1978a, b] ***** 将这些加上 Backus-Letter_to_Dana_Scott-1978_09_14.pdf 添加到参考文献，第 1 部分。

当埃兹格·迪杰斯特拉 (Edsger Dijkstra) 在他的个人 EWD 系列中将巴科斯的讲座评论为第 692 号时，一场更有活力的交流开始了，该演讲直接分发给迪杰斯特拉的大约十几位朋友，但间接传播给了包括巴科斯在内的更多观众。 它的结论相对平淡[Dijkstra1978b]：

“简而言之，这篇文章是一份关于有效研究工作的进展报告，但在取得令人信服的结果之前很久就严重夸大了其重要性。 更令人遗憾的是，它是通过图灵奖讲座的方式发表的。”

但完整的评论相当负面，并引发了巴科斯和迪杰斯特拉之间的信件往来[Chin2016]，其中迪杰斯特拉宣称他的评论是一本“政治小册子”，旨在反驳他显然认为巴克斯对迪杰斯特拉、霍尔和其他人正在开发的公理语义的攻击。

到 2026 年，ACM 数字图书馆记录了超过 2000 次对 [Backus1978b] 的引用，而且还在不断增加。 尽管绝大多数人似乎都引用这篇论文作为“冯·诺依曼架构”的参考，但许多论文，尤其是在第一个十年，都是以各种方式应用或扩展巴科斯思想的真正尝试：

  • 扩展程序算法：Banerjee，...
  • 优化转换：Bellegarde、Norman...
  • 实现：Baden、Choppy 等人、Robinson、Biagionni、Valencia、Deleuze。
  • 并行计算：Ben-Asher 等人、Christopher 和 Ameiss
  • 数据库查询：Bossi 和 Ghezzi、Buneman 和 Frankel
  • 流处理：Ida 和 Tanaka、Sheeran、Shultis、Thomas 和 Stanat
  • 惰性评估：Dosch 和 Möller、Radensky
  • VLSI 设计：Sheeran、Tsanakas 等人。
  • 数据流机：Zhang 等人。
  • 还有更多 - 请参阅参考资料，第 2 部分

激发和完善代数

自从 1975 年我转向 System R 项目以来，巴科斯就一直独自工作。 1978 年 7 月，约翰·海登·威廉姆斯 (John Hayden Williams) 加入他的行列。 威廉姆斯在威斯康星大学麦迪逊分校获得博士学位，其论文题为“有界上下文可解析语法”。 他加入康奈尔大学任教，在那里进行编程语言研究。 在某个时候，他遇到了约翰·巴克斯 (John Backus)，后者在 [Backus1973a] 和 [Backus1978b] 的致谢中提到了他。 也许加入 IBM 的想法是在 1977 年 12 月讨论的，当时 Backus 在康奈尔大学发表演讲 [Backus2003，第 159 项]。

巴科斯和威廉姆斯开始致力于改进程序的代数。 那年夏天，威廉姆斯是德国马克托贝尔多夫一年一度的北约暑期学校的讲师之一。 Dijkstra 报道 [Dijkstra1978a]：

“最后一天的最后一场讲座——关于还原语言——是由其中一位参与者 John H. Williams（正在从康奈尔大学转到 IBM 的过程中？ 圣何塞）。 这是一场精彩的演讲，演讲有力。 鉴于参与者是暑期学校中最出色的部分，我们非常希望有一个更合适的闭幕讲座。”

1979 年 8 月，巴克斯在加州大学圣克鲁斯分校编程方法论夏季研讨会上提交了一份论文草稿 [Backus1979]。 与他的图灵奖演讲一样，他用了很多篇幅将他的函数式方法与“冯·诺依曼语言”进行比较。 他的方法是关注形式语义。 在具有语句、赋值和副作用的命令式语言中，语句（或具有副作用的表达式）的含义必须建模为将存储（内存状态）映射到存储的函数，而函数式程序是将值（输入）映射到值（输出）的函数。 尽管他向读者保证他不是在建立一个“稻草人”，但他对命令式语言的指称语义的非正式描述是用尖刻的风格写的。 他得出的结论是，使用四种主要组合形式（常量、组合、条件和构造）的函数式程序要强大得多，因为存在与这些组合形式相互关联的程序代数。 当然，命令式语言具有这些组合形式的类似物：常量、用于排序语句的复合表达式和分号、条件表达式和语句以及局部变量，但无可否认，命令式语言的正确性和等价性证明通常需要完整的谓词逻辑，而不是巴科斯提倡的等式风格。 公平地说，巴克斯指出了阻碍采用函数式风格的两个问题：“命名”（当需要跟踪大量数量时，变量很有用）和“遗忘”（用函数模拟变量会带来存储）。 论文的第二部分进一步发展了他在图灵奖演讲中的“线性展开定理”。

其他人的实施

Scott Baden 的 Berkeley FP 是用 Franz Lisp 编写的解释器，并随 Berkeley Unix 的多个版本一起发布；参见 [BadenPatel198x]、[Baden1983a–c]。

Arch Robinson 的伊利诺伊州 FP 也是用 C 语言编写的解释器；它是通过 USENET 新闻组 comp.sources.unix 分发的。 参见[Robinson1987a-e]。

爱德华·S。 Biagioni的FPC是用C语言编写的；将 FP 翻译为 C，然后用 C 编译器进行编译； 1.0 版通过 USENET 新闻组 comp.sources.unix 分发。 参见[Biagioni1988]。

Andy Valencia 的斯坦福 FP 是一个用 C 语言编写的解释器，并通过 USENET 新闻组 comp.sources.unix 分发。 参见[巴伦西亚1986]。

Christophe Deleuze 的 oc-FP 是用 OCaml 编写的解释器，并通过 Deleuze 的网站分发。 参见[Deleuze2003]。
